entries.title: Ask your own questions on a Call for Reviewers application
entries.summary: A Call for Reviewers interest form can now ask your own questions: short text, long text, one choice or several choices, each optionally required. Add them under **Settings → Questions**; applicants answer under **More about you**, the people list shows their **Answers**, and each applicant is added to your organization's **Contacts** (when the organization has a default contact record type).

where.path: Awards → program → Call for reviewers → Settings → Questions; Program → Evaluation → Call for reviewers → Settings → Questions; public application link

entries.use_case: Programs that recruit judges can collect what they need to place them (years of judging, specialties, region) on the application itself, instead of a separate survey, and find applicants in their CRM afterwards (organizations with a default contact record type, which is nearly all).

cs_action.note: Customers who asked for a judges application form (SB-7451) can now add their own questions; the applicants land in CRM Contacts.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer recruits judges or reviewers and wants extra questions on the application, or asks where applicants show up in the CRM.
internal.who_should_get_it: Awards and evaluation customers running a Call for Reviewers.
internal.staff_path: Awards → program → Call for reviewers → Settings → Questions
internal.gotchas: Up to 20 questions per call. Renaming a question or an option keeps existing answers; removing a question hides its answers. A contact is only created when the org has a default Contacts record type. An org-level call across programs is not built yet; Add from reviewer pool brings judges from other programs.
internal.talk_track: Open the call's Settings, add your questions under Questions, and share the public link. Answers show on the people list next to each applicant.

entries.title: Due reminders follow the event's time zone and keep coming after the event's dates
entries.summary: The 7-day and 1-day due reminders now count days in the event's time zone, and they go to evaluators with reviews left even when the event's own dates have already passed.
entries.use_case: Awards and post-event reviews keep their reminders, and a round that closes on the 24th reminds on the 23rd wherever the event is.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports evaluators did not get a due-soon reminder.
internal.staff_path: Program → Evaluation → plan → Rounds → Review closes
internal.gotchas: The weekly summary still stops 7 days after the event ends.
internal.talk_track: Reminders go out 7 days and 1 day before the plan due date or a round's Review closes, in the event's time zone.

entries.title: Narrow who is on a live Advocacy campaign
entries.summary: When you edit a campaign's recipients in **Select** mode, **When applying** now offers **Add to existing**, **Replace not yet engaged** and **Replace all**. Replace modes show exactly how many people will be removed before anything changes; removed people lose their console link without being notified, and their past shares stay in your reports.

where.path: Marketing → Advocacy → campaign → Edit campaign → Recipients → Select

entries.use_case: A campaign launched to all speakers can be cut down to, say, accepted speakers only, without removing people one by one or rebuilding the campaign.

cs_action.note: A CS ticket asked for this (linked on the Jira story); follow up there.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer launched an Advocacy campaign to the wrong people and wants to correct the audience.
internal.who_should_get_it: Advocacy customers who launch to all speakers before their program is final.
internal.staff_path: Event → Marketing → Advocacy → campaign → Edit campaign → Recipients → Select → When applying
internal.gotchas: Only for hand-picked (Select) campaigns; All and By portal audiences are live and update themselves. Engaged = shared, downloaded or opened their console. Already-posted share links keep redirecting.
internal.talk_track: Set the filter, pick Replace not yet engaged so anyone who already shared keeps their card, check the count and confirm.

entries.title: Attendee Advocacy: clearer recipient picker, named Notify emails, My sessions
entries.summary: The attendee picker shows each person's email and company (nameless attendees by email); Notify emails open with each recipient's first name via `{{first_name}}`, and the Notify and Export dialogs follow the admin language. Attendees see **My sessions**, the sessions they're registered for, on their console, and uploaded headshots keep showing after a reload.
entries.use_case: Attendee campaigns read as personal: the email greets people by name and their console lists the sessions they're going to.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer runs an Attendees or Speakers Advocacy campaign.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers running Attendees or Speakers Advocacy campaigns.
internal.staff_path: Event → Marketing → Advocacy → campaign → Notify recipients
internal.gotchas: My sessions needs session registrations synced (Cvent session sync, Pathways session fill or Attend reservations). Speaker share-link previews on LinkedIn now say '<Name> invited you to <event>'.
internal.talk_track: Send Notify as is: each email starts with the person's first name.

entries.title: Charge accepted submissions only
entries.summary: Session submission forms have a third payment option, **Upon Acceptance**: nothing is collected at submission, and when a submission is accepted its submitter is asked to pay the form's fee. Add `{{{submission_fee_link}}}`, `{{submission_fee_amount}}` and `{{submission_fee_due_date}}` to your acceptance email.

enable.path: Program → Collect & Review → Forms → form → Payments & Fees → When to Collect Payment → Upon Acceptance

where.path: Form builder → Payments & Fees; the acceptance email's merge tags; the submitter's payment page; session → Connections

entries.use_case: Associations and medical societies that charge a presentation fee only to accepted speakers can collect it in Sessionboard instead of invoicing outside it, without charging everyone who submits.

cs_action.note: American Medical Association asked for this (SB-10392). The form needs a payment gateway; the acceptance email must include the new merge tags.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer charges speakers a fee only after acceptance, or refunds rejected submitters today.
internal.who_should_get_it: Session submission form customers with a payment gateway who charge accepted speakers.
internal.staff_path: Program → Collect & Review → Forms → form → Payments & Fees
internal.gotchas: The submitter pays once per submission (not each speaker). Accepted means the session status, not participant acceptance. Payable after the CFP deadline; the due date is informational. Refunds stay manual from Invoices; withdrawing an accepted session does not refund. Unpaid fees are not listed on the Invoices page until paid; check the session's Connections tab. Awards does not have this option yet.
internal.talk_track: Pick Upon Acceptance on the form's Payments & Fees step, set the fee and an optional due date, then add the submission fee merge tags to the email you send accepted speakers. Only the submitter sees the pay link.
